rationale: Members cover glycogen synthesis, breakdown, glycophagy and GSD 0, II, IV, XV and Lafora (plus GCK MODY), distinguishing from glucose-6-phosphatase GSD I and glycolysis themes.

name: Lung branching, mesenchyme and trachea development
rationale: All members concern lung bud branching, lung mesenchyme proliferation, lobe, vasculature and trachea development, distinguishing them from salivary/limb bud and alveolar saccule/pneumocyte confusables.

name: Lung branching morphogenesis, mesenchyme and trachea development
rationale: All members concern lung bud branching, lung mesenchyme and epithelial proliferation, lobe, vasculature and tracheal formation, unlike salivary/limb epithelial-mesenchymal confusables and the alveolar pneumocyte confusable.

name: Lung branching morphogenesis, mesenchymal growth and trachea formation
rationale: All members concern early lung and trachea organogenesis (branching, bud elongation, mesenchymal proliferation, vasculature), whereas confusables add limb/salivary epithelial-mesenchymal signaling or later saccular and pneumocyte differentiation.

qualifier: BAX/BAK effector step and downstream apoptosome/SMAC
name: BAX/BAK outer membrane permeabilization to apoptosome caspase activation
rationale: Members run from BAX/BAK activation and MOMP/cytochrome c release to apoptosome caspase activation and SMAC-IAP release, whereas confusables centre on upstream BH3-only protein activation.

name: Mitochondrial apoptosis execution via BAX/BAK, apoptosome and SMAC
rationale: Members run from BAX/BAK outer-membrane permeabilization and cytochrome c release to apoptosome caspase activation and SMAC antagonism of IAPs; confusables centre on upstream BH3-only protein activation.

qualifier: BAX/BAK permeabilization through apoptosome and SMAC-IAP caspase activation
name: BAX/BAK outer membrane permeabilization to apoptosome caspase activation
rationale: Members run from BAX/BAK oligomerisation and MOMP regulation through cytochrome c release to apoptosome and SMAC/IAP control of caspases, whereas confusables centre on upstream BH3-only protein activation.

name: Epithelial plasma membrane solute carriers and cystine transport
rationale: Members are plasma-membrane transporter modules plus cystine transport and its cystinuria defects, whereas confusables are neutral amino acid, peptide or urate transport.

name: Epithelial solute carrier transport with cystine reabsorption
rationale: Members are plasma-membrane SLC transporter modules of liver and kidney epithelia plus cystine transport and cystinuria, distinguishing it from neutral amino acid, peptide and urate transport confusables.

name: Plasma membrane solute carriers with renal cystine transport
rationale: Members are plasma-membrane/SLC transporter gene modules plus L-cystine transport and its cystinuria defects, unlike confusables built on neutral amino acid, proline/glycine, peptide or urate transport.

qualifier: IL-17/Th17 with IL-33, IL-36 and IL-38
name: IL-17/Th17 and IL-33/IL-36/IL-38 cytokine signaling
rationale: Members are IL-17 production/signaling, Th17 commitment and IL-33, IL-36 and IL-38 signaling, separating it from Dectin/antifungal, IL-1/IL-18 processing and IL-12/IL-23 neighbours.

name: IL-17/Th17 and IL-33, IL-36, IL-38 cytokine signaling
rationale: Members cover IL-17 production/signaling and Th17 commitment plus IL-1-family IL-33/IL-36/IL-38 signaling, separating it from IL-18/IL-1 processing, IL-12/23/10 and Dectin neighbours.

name: IL-17 and IL-33/IL-36/IL-38 cytokine signaling
rationale: Members are IL-17/Th17 signaling plus IL-33, IL-36 and IL-38 signaling; the IL-33 members distinguish it from IL-1/IL-18 and IL-23/antifungal confusables.

qualifier: gastrointestinal and urinary tract, stomach function
name: Gastrointestinal and urinary tract motility and stomach function
rationale: Members cover peristalsis, gastric and intestinal smooth muscle contraction, micturition, gastric acid secretion and stomach development, distinct from confusables on enteric nervous system development, general smooth muscle relaxation and reproductive smooth muscle.

name: Gastric function and gut and urinary smooth muscle motility
rationale: Members concern stomach function, peristalsis, GI and urinary tract smooth muscle contraction and micturition, unlike confusables on enteric nervous system development, generic smooth muscle relaxation or reproductive smooth muscle.

name: Gut and urinary tract smooth muscle motility
rationale: Members concern peristalsis, gastric motility, intestinal and urinary tract smooth muscle contraction and micturition plus stomach function, unlike confusables on enteric nervous system development, general smooth muscle relaxation or reproductive smooth muscle.

name: Calcium- and cAMP-driven CREB phosphorylation and CaMKK-AMPK signaling
rationale: All members are Ca2+/calmodulin-kinase or cAMP cascades carrying postsynaptic signals to CREB or AMPK; the CaMKK-AMPK arm and the absence of synaptic-plasticity/LTP and PKA-activation terms separate it from the confusables.

name: Calcium- and cAMP-driven CREB phosphorylation and CAMKK-AMPK signaling
rationale: All members concern CaMK/adenylate cyclase kinase cascades relaying postsynaptic calcium to CREB or AMPK, lacking the NMDA/AMPA receptor, LTP and memory members of C1/C2/C4 and the PKA-only focus of C3.

core: Neuronal calcium and cAMP signalling to CREB
name: Neuronal calcium-cAMP signalling to CREB and AMPK
rationale: All members describe synaptic calcium/cAMP second-messenger signalling via CaMK and adenylate cyclase to CREB, and the CaMKK-AMPK branch distinguishes it from the synaptic plasticity, memory and NMDA receptor confusables.

qualifier: PLC and beta-arrestin routes and synaptic modulation
name: Dopaminergic synaptic modulation via PLC and beta-arrestin signalling
rationale: Members are non-cAMP dopamine receptor signalling (PLC-activating, beta-arrestin) with dopamine release and synaptic modulation, unlike confusables centred on adenylate cyclase-coupled dopamine receptors or drug responses.

qualifier: PLC- and beta-arrestin-coupled dopamine receptor signalling
name: Dopaminergic transmission via PLC and beta-arrestin receptor signalling
rationale: Members regulate dopaminergic synaptic transmission and dopamine receptor signalling via phospholipase C and beta-arrestin, whereas confusables carry adenylate cyclase-coupled dopamine receptor signalling and drug behaviours.

qualifier: dopamine release and cAMP-independent receptor signalling
name: Dopamine release and cAMP-independent dopamine receptor signalling
rationale: Members concern dopaminergic transmission, dopamine secretion and PLC/beta-arrestin dopamine receptor signalling, whereas confusables carry adenylate cyclase-coupled dopamine receptors or drug-response behaviours.

name: Sphingomyelin hydrolysis and ceramide homeostasis regulation
rationale: Members concern sphingomyelinase-driven ceramide production and regulation of ceramide/sphingolipid levels; confusables cover glycosphingolipid metabolism, ER-Golgi lipid transfer or de novo sphingolipid synthesis.

name: Regulation of ceramide levels and sphingomyelin breakdown
rationale: All members regulate sphingolipid/ceramide levels, with TNFR1-induced sphingomyelin hydrolysis distinguishing it from glycosphingolipid, de novo synthesis and lipid transfer confusables.

name: Sphingomyelin-derived ceramide and sphingolipid homeostasis regulation
rationale: Members regulate ceramide levels via sphingomyelin hydrolysis and feedback on sphingolipid synthesis, versus confusables on de novo sphingolipid biosynthesis, glycosphingolipids or lipid transfer.

name: Retroviral integration, viral latency and retroelement silencing
rationale: Members cover HIV entry, reverse transcription and integration, viral transcription/latency (HIV, HCMV) and KRAB-ZFP/HUSH silencing of endogenous retroelements, the latter distinguishing it from RNA-virus and APOBEC-editing confusables.

core: Viral DNA integration and transcriptional latency
name: Viral DNA integration, latency and host retroelement silencing
rationale: Members cover retroviral reverse transcription and integration, herpesvirus events, host control of viral transcription and latency, and HUSH/KRAB-ZFP silencing of retroelements, which separate it from RNA-virus replication and APOBEC editing confusables.

name: Retroviral integration, viral latency and host silencing of retroelements
rationale: Members cover HIV entry, reverse transcription and integration, HCMV events, latency and host HUSH/KRAB-ZFP/ChAHP silencing of viral and endogenous retroelement transcription; the silencing and latency members distinguish it from APOBEC editing and RNA-virus neighbours.

name: Dolichyl-phosphate and GDP-mannose donor synthesis
rationale: Members concern synthesis of dolichyl phosphate, GDP-mannose and dolichyl-phosphate mannose and the corresponding CDGs (DOLK, DPM1-3, MPI, PMM2, PGM1, DHDDS, SRD5A3), unlike neighbours on GPI anchors, UDP-GlcNAc/sialic acid or ALG oligosaccharide assembly.

name: GDP-mannose and dolichyl-phosphate mannose synthesis and disorders
rationale: Members are synthesis of GDP-mannose, dolichyl-phosphate and Dol-P-Man and their CDG defects (PMM2, MPI, DPM1-3, DOLK, SRD5A3), upstream of the ALG/GPI/UDP-sugar steps in confusables.

name: GDP-mannose and dolichyl-phosphate-mannose donor synthesis
rationale: Members concern synthesis of GDP-mannose, dolichyl phosphate and dolichyl-phosphate mannose and the CDGs from their enzymes; distinct from ALG oligosaccharide assembly, GPI anchor and UDP-GlcNAc/sialic acid confusables.

qualifier: FRS2 and SHC cascades from FGFR1 and FGFR4
name: FRS2 and SHC MAPK signaling from FGFR1 and FGFR4
rationale: Members are the FRS- and SHC-adaptor routes to MAPK downstream of FGFR1 and FGFR4, distinguishing them from FGFR2/FGFR3 adaptor cascades and the PLC-gamma and PI3K branches.

qualifier: FGFR1 and FGFR4 via FRS2 and SHC
name: FGFR1 and FGFR4 FRS2/SHC adaptor signaling to MAPK
rationale: Members are FRS- and SHC-mediated MAPK cascades of FGFR1 and FGFR4 with betaKlotho co-receptor binding, separating it from FGFR2/FGFR3 cascades and PLC or PI3K branches in the confusables.

name: FRS2/SHC-mediated MAPK signaling by FGFR1 and FGFR4
rationale: Members are FRS- and SHC-driven MAPK cascades from FGFR1 and FGFR4 (with beta-Klotho ligand binding), distinct from PI3K/PLC branches and FGFR2/FGFR3 confusables.

qualifier: positive regulation of polymerization at the leading edge
name: Actin polymerization-driven leading-edge protrusion in cell migration
rationale: All members promote actin polymerization and lamellipodium/pseudopodium extension at the leading edge of migrating cells, whereas confusables concern actin severing/depolymerization, negative regulation of migration or Arp2/3-WAVE nucleation.

name: Promotion of actin-driven leading-edge protrusion in migration
rationale: All members promote actin polymerization, lamellipodia/pseudopodia and leading-edge localization for motility, unlike confusables about Arp2/3-WAVE nucleation, filament severing/capping or negative regulation of migration.

name: Actin-driven leading-edge protrusion in migrating cells
rationale: All members promote actin polymerisation, lamellipodia, pseudopodia and leading-edge localisation for motility, unlike confusables about negative regulation of migration, WASP/WAVE-Arp2/3 nucleation, or actin severing and depolymerisation.

name: Non-vesicular phospholipid transfer at ER membrane contacts
rationale: Members describe ER tethering/localization and intermembrane transfer of phospholipids such as PI and PC; confusables instead concern sphingolipid metabolism, ER tubule shaping, flippases or glycolipid transport.

name: Phospholipid transfer at ER membrane contact sites
rationale: Members describe intermembrane PI/PC transfer and ER tethering/localization at contact sites; confusables instead cover flippase translocation, sphingolipid or glycolipid transport, or ER tubular network shaping without lipid transfer.

name: Phospholipid transfer at ER membrane contact sites
rationale: Members cover non-vesicular phospholipid (PI/PC) transfer between the ER and other membranes plus ER positioning and ER-plasma membrane tethering, distinguishing it from ER tubular-network shaping, sphingolipid metabolism, flippase translocation and glycolipid transport.

name: Dopamine receptor signaling via adenylate cyclase and beta-arrestin
rationale: Members are dopamine receptor signaling through adenylate cyclase and beta-arrestin and its locomotor output, unlike confusables on dopamine synthesis, transport, addiction or PLC coupling.

name: Dopamine receptor signaling via adenylyl cyclase and beta-arrestin
rationale: Members are dopamine receptor signaling (cAMP-coupled and beta-arrestin) and its locomotor output, unlike confusables on dopaminergic transmission, drug responses, PLC-coupled signaling or dopamine synthesis/transport.

name: Dopamine receptor signaling via adenylate cyclase and beta-arrestin
rationale: Members are dopamine receptor signaling through adenylate cyclase or beta-arrestin and locomotor regulation, unlike confusables on PLC-coupled signaling, dopamine synthesis/transport or drug-related behaviour.

name: Histone and DNA methylation in epigenetic gene silencing
rationale: Members are histone lysine/arginine methylation and demethylation, DNA/CpG methylation and their silencing outcomes (imprinting, X inactivation, facultative heterochromatin), unlike CHD/NuRD/HDAC remodeling confusables.

name: Histone and DNA methylation in heterochromatin silencing and imprinting
rationale: Members are histone lysine/arginine methylation and demethylation, DNA/CpG methylation and their outputs (X inactivation, imprinting, facultative heterochromatin), unlike confusables built on CHD/NuRD remodelling or RUNX1/E2F6 co-factors.

qualifier: epigenetic silencing, imprinting and X inactivation
name: Protein and DNA methylation in epigenetic gene silencing
rationale: Members cover histone/protein lysine and arginine methylation, demethylation and DNA methylation with heterochromatin, imprinting and X inactivation; confusables emphasise CHD/NuRD remodeling, deacetylation or arginine-only methylation.

name: Caspase-8 extrinsic apoptosis and TRIF/RIPK1 necroptosis
rationale: Members cover FAS/TRAIL-driven procaspase-8 activation, c-FLIP and BID, plus TLR3/TRIF- and RIPK1-mediated necroptosis, which separates it from T-cell activation-induced death and TBK1/IRF3 confusables.

core: Caspase-8 and RIPK1 regulated cell death
qualifier: triggered by death receptors and TLR3-TRIF, including necroptosis
name: Death receptor and TLR3-TRIF caspase-8 apoptosis and necroptosis
rationale: Members cover Fas/TRAIL extrinsic apoptosis via procaspase-8 dimerization, c-FLIP and BID, plus TRIF/TLR3- and microbe-modulated RIPK1 necroptosis, which separates the theme from T cell activation-induced death and TBK1/IRF3 confusables.

qualifier: death receptor apoptosis and TRIF/RIPK1 necroptosis
name: Caspase-8 death receptor apoptosis and TRIF-driven necroptosis
rationale: Members are TRAIL and FasL death receptor signalling, procaspase-8 activation, c-FLIP, BID cleavage and TLR3/TRIF- or microbe-modulated RIPK1 necroptosis, unlike neighbours about T cell activation-induced death, TLR3-IRF3 signalling or necrosis regulation.

name: Semaphorin-plexin signaling via Sema3A and Sema4D
rationale: All members are semaphorin-plexin pathways (Sema3A repulsion, Sema4D growth-cone collapse, RND1, CRMPs), distinguishing them from confusables built on general axon guidance, netrin, ephrin or Rho-GPCR signaling.

qualifier: Sema3A and Sema4D repulsion and growth-cone collapse
name: Semaphorin-plexin repulsive signaling via Sema3A and Sema4D
rationale: Every member is semaphorin-plexin signaling (Sema3A via CRMPs, PAK and integrin inhibition; Sema4D via RND1 and cell-migration inhibition), distinguishing it from netrin/ephrin axon guidance and Rho-GPCR confusables.

name: Sema3A and Sema4D plexin repulsive signaling
rationale: All members are semaphorin-plexin signalling events (including RND1 binding plexins) causing growth-cone collapse and loss of adhesion, whereas confusables are general axon guidance, ephrin, netrin or G12/13-Rho signalling.

qualifier: pseudouridylation and methylation across rRNA, tRNA, mRNA
name: Pseudouridylation and methylation of rRNA, tRNA and mRNA
rationale: All members are pseudouridine synthesis or methylation of cytosolic RNAs, whereas confusables are tRNA aminoacylation, mitochondrial RNA processing or snoRNP assembly.

qualifier: pseudouridylation and methylation across rRNA, tRNA, mRNA
name: Pseudouridylation and methylation of rRNA, tRNA and mRNA
rationale: All members are pseudouridine or methyl modifications of cytoplasmic/nuclear RNAs; confusables involve snoRNP assembly, mitochondrial RNA modification or tRNA aminoacylation and processing.

name: tRNA, rRNA and mRNA methylation and pseudouridylation
rationale: Members are base and 2'-O methylation and pseudouridine synthesis on tRNA, rRNA and mRNA, distinct from snoRNP assembly, mitochondrial RNA modification and tRNA processing/aminoacylation confusables.

name: Golgi ribbon disassembly, reassembly and positioning
rationale: All members concern Golgi architecture: ribbon formation, mitotic disassembly/reassembly and pericentriolar localization, unlike confusables on Golgi vesicle budding, intra-Golgi traffic or unrelated GTPase cycles.

qualifier: ribbon disassembly, reassembly and pericentriolar positioning
name: Golgi ribbon disassembly, reassembly and pericentriolar positioning
rationale: All members concern Golgi ribbon structure and positioning (disassembly, reassembly, pericentriolar stacking, kinectin-mediated localization), unlike confusables about intra-Golgi traffic, vesicle budding or other Rho GTPase effectors.

name: Golgi ribbon disassembly, reassembly and positioning
rationale: All members concern the architecture of the Golgi (ribbon formation, mitotic disassembly/reassembly, pericentriolar positioning), distinguishing the theme from confusables on intra-Golgi vesicle traffic, secretion and Rho-family GTPase cycles.

name: TNFR1 signaling to canonical NF-kappaB activation
rationale: All members concern TNFR1-initiated signaling, its linear-ubiquitin step and positive canonical NF-kappaB output, unlike the noncanonical NIK arm, TLR/IRAK-driven IKK recruitment, or the negative-regulation-of-death neighbour.

name: TNFR1 signaling promoting canonical NF-kappaB activation
rationale: Members cover TNFR1-induced NF-kappaB and proapoptotic signaling with LUBAC linear ubiquitination and positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB, unlike confusables focused on negative regulation of death-receptor necrosis, TLR/IRAK-driven IKK recruitment, or non-canonical NIK signaling.

name: TNFR1-driven canonical NF-kB activation and linear ubiquitination
rationale: All members concern TNFR1 signaling and positive canonical NF-kB activation (with LUBAC linear ubiquitination), unlike confusables built on RIP1/IRAK1 IKK recruitment, negative TNF/necroptosis regulation, or noncanonical NF-kB.

qualifier: M-CSF-driven monocyte, macrophage and dendritic cell
name: M-CSF signaling in monocyte, macrophage and dendritic cell development
rationale: Members concern M-CSF signalling and the differentiation and proliferation of monocytes, macrophages and myeloid dendritic cells, unlike confusables on granulocyte/G-CSF development or generic interleukin SHC signalling.

name: M-CSF-driven monocyte, macrophage and dendritic cell development
rationale: Members are M-CSF signalling and positive regulation of monocyte, macrophage and myeloid DC differentiation and proliferation, unlike granulocyte/G-CSF themes or negative regulation of myeloid differentiation.

name: M-CSF-driven monocyte, macrophage and dendritic cell differentiation
rationale: Members concern M-CSF signaling and the differentiation/proliferation of monocytes, macrophages and myeloid DCs, whereas confusables centre on granulocyte/neutrophil differentiation or CSF1 receptor signaling without differentiation.

qualifier: phorbol ester, lipid and VEGF receptor inputs
name: Protein kinase C signalling from lipid and VEGF receptors
rationale: Members concern PKC regulation, phorbol ester response, PKC-zeta and PI synthesis downstream of LPA/S1P and VEGFR2 receptors, distinguishing it from confusables on calcium/cAMP GPCR signalling or BCR signalling.

name: Protein kinase C signaling and phorbol ester response
rationale: Members converge on PKC activation by phorbol ester, phosphoinositide/lipid receptors, VEGFR2 and estrogen via PRKCZ, whereas confusables emphasize G protein calcium, cAMP, BCR or Wnt-calcium signaling.

qualifier: from lipid and growth factor receptors
name: Protein kinase C signalling from lipid and growth factor receptors
rationale: Members converge on PKC activity (phorbol ester response, PKC regulation, PRKCZ) triggered by LPA/sphingolipid receptors, VEGFR2 and estrogen, whereas neighbours centre on G-protein calcium/IP3, cAMP or BCR signalling.

qualifier: STRA6, LRAT and RDH12 loss of function
name: Retinoid metabolism disease from STRA6, LRAT, RDH12 loss
rationale: Members are vitamin A metabolism and its disease events caused by STRA6, LRAT and RDH12 defects, unlike confusables on the rod/cone retinoid cycle (ABCA4, RDH5) or retinoic acid synthesis.

qualifier: retinol uptake and esterification defects impairing phototransduction
name: Vitamin A metabolism defects causing retinal phototransduction disease
rationale: Members are vitamin A metabolism and its disease events, specifically STRA6, LRAT and RDH12 loss-of-function defects of visual phototransduction, distinct from the rod/cone retinoid cycle and retinoic acid metabolism confusables.

qualifier: retinol uptake and esterification defects impairing vision
name: Vitamin A metabolism defects impairing visual phototransduction
rationale: Members are vitamin A metabolism and its disease events, namely visual phototransduction defects from STRA6, LRAT and RDH12 loss, distinct from the rod/cone retinoid cycle and retinoic acid metabolism neighbours.

core: Centrosome and microtubule organizing centre organization
qualifier: centriole duplication, spindle orientation and cilium dynamics
name: Centrosome, centriole duplication, spindle orientation and cilium dynamics
rationale: Members concern centriole duplication and cohesion, MTOC nucleation and anchoring, spindle positioning and cilium assembly/disassembly; confusables are mitotic centrosome maturation or tubulin modification.

qualifier: centriole duplication, cilium dynamics and spindle positioning
name: Centriole, cilium and spindle-positioning microtubule organization
rationale: Members regulate centriole duplication and cohesion, MTOC nucleation and anchoring, cilium assembly and disassembly and spindle orientation, separating them from mitotic centrosome-maturation and tubulin-modification neighbours.

qualifier: centriole duplication, spindle positioning and ciliogenesis
name: Centrosome control of spindle positioning, centriole duplication and cilia
rationale: Members are MTOC microtubule nucleation/anchoring, centriole duplication and cohesion, spindle orientation and asymmetric division, and cilium assembly/disassembly; confusables are mitotic centrosome maturation (AURKA, NuMA) and tubulin modification.

qualifier: factor VIII, IX and V defects
name: Intrinsic coagulation with factor VIII, IX and V defects
rationale: Members are coagulation cascade initiation/propagation and many defective F8, F9 and FV variants, whereas confusables emphasise fibrin formation, fibrinolysis, VWF and platelet activation.

qualifier: factor V, VIII and IX defects
name: Intrinsic coagulation cascade with factor V, VIII, IX defects
rationale: Members are the coagulation cascade (initiation, intrinsic and common pathways) and many defective F8, F9 and FV variants, which the fibrin, fibrinolysis, VWF and FXII confusables lack.

qualifier: factor VIII, IX and V variant defects
name: Coagulation cascade with factor VIII, IX and V defects
rationale: Members are the intrinsic/common coagulation cascade and many defective F8, F9 and FV variant events, which fibrinolysis- and VWF-focused confusables lack.

qualifier: transferrin, ferroportin and heme uptake and transport
name: Iron and heme transport in systemic iron homeostasis
rationale: Members cover transferrin cycling, iron import/export defects (SLC11A2, SLC40A1, ceruloplasmin) and heme scavenging, distinguishing them from heme biosynthesis, other-metal transport and scavenger-receptor confusables.

qualifier: transferrin and heme uptake and transport
name: Iron and heme uptake, transport and homeostasis
rationale: Members cover iron import/export disorders, transferrin cycling and heme scavenging/transport, separating it from copper/manganese, heme biosynthesis and scavenger receptor confusables.

qualifier: iron and heme uptake and transport
name: Iron and heme uptake, transport and systemic homeostasis
rationale: Members concern transferrin/iron import, ferroportin and DMT1 disorders, heme scavenging and transport, unlike confusables on other metals, scavenger receptors or heme biosynthesis.

name: Cardiac chamber myocardium and ventricular septum morphogenesis
rationale: All members describe ventricular and atrial myocardium development (trabeculae, compact myocardium), and only this theme includes membranous and muscular septum morphogenesis.

name: Ventricular myocardium and cardiac septum morphogenesis
rationale: Members concern morphogenesis of ventricular trabecular and compact myocardium and the membranous and muscular septum, which the early cardiogenesis and cardiomyocyte proliferation confusables lack.

name: Cardiac chamber myocardium and septum morphogenesis
rationale: Members concern trabecular/compact ventricular and atrial myocardium plus muscular and membranous septum morphogenesis, while confusables cover early heart-tube specification or cardiomyocyte proliferation and hypertrophy.

name: Thyroid hormone synthesis, action and peroxide generation
rationale: Members cover thyroid hormone generation (including the H2O2/ROS supply), transport, activity and receptor response, distinct from confusables on ascorbate, sulfate/iodide anion transport or selenium metabolism.

name: Thyroid hormone synthesis, H2O2 generation and receptor signaling
rationale: Members cover thyroid hormone generation, transport and receptor responses with the hydrogen peroxide production it requires, unlike confusables on selenium, sulfate/iodide transport or ascorbate.

name: Thyroid hormone synthesis, signaling and peroxide generation
rationale: Members span thyroid hormone generation, transport and receptor signaling plus H2O2/ROS production used in hormone synthesis, separating it from selenium, sulfonation, vitamin C and anion-transporter themes.

qualifier: PAPS and nucleotide-sugar synthesis and transport
name: PAPS sulfate donor and nucleotide-sugar synthesis and transport
rationale: Members concern PAPS and UDP-sugar formation and transport and their skeletal dysplasias (PAPSS2, SLC26A2, SLC35D1), unlike GAG biosynthesis, selenium and SLC35 CDG confusables.

qualifier: PAPS and nucleotide-sugar transport with chondrodysplasias
name: PAPS and nucleotide-sugar donor supply and skeletal chondrodysplasias
rationale: Members concern producing and transporting PAPS, sulfate and nucleotide sugars (PAPSS2, SLC26A2, SLC35D1, UDP-glucuronate) whose defects cause chondrodysplasias, distinguishing it from GAG chain synthesis, selenocysteine and SLC35 CDG confusables.

qualifier: PAPS synthesis/transport and nucleotide-sugar transport in skeletal dysplasias
name: Activated sulfate and nucleotide-sugar donor supply in chondrodysplasias
rationale: Members are PAPS synthesis/transport, UDP-glucuronate formation, nucleotide-sugar and sulfate transport and their chondrodysplasias, unlike confusables on GAG chain biosynthesis, selenium metabolism or SLC35 CDGs.

qualifier: activation by BH3-only proteins PUMA, NOXA and BAD
name: BH3-only protein activation of BAX/BAK cytochrome c release
rationale: All members describe BH3-only proteins (PUMA, NOXA, BAD) neutralising anti-apoptotic BCL-2 members and activating BAX/BAK to release cytochrome c, whereas confusables centre on MOMP regulation in general, p53 transcription, or downstream apoptosome/SMAC events.

core: Mitochondrial apoptosis initiation by BCL-2 family proteins
qualifier: BH3-only and BAX/BAK activation at mitochondria
name: BH3-only and BAX/BAK activation at mitochondria
rationale: All members are BCL-2-family steps (BH3-only BAD/NOXA/PUMA translocation, BAX/BAK oligomerization, BCL-2 inactivation) driving cytochrome c release, upstream of the apoptosome/SMAC and p53-transcriptional events in the confusables.

core: BH3-only protein activation of BAX/BAK at mitochondria
name: NOXA/PUMA/BAD-driven BAX/BAK activation and cytochrome c release
rationale: All members concern BH3-only proteins (NOXA, PUMA, BAD) inactivating anti-apoptotic BCL-2 members and activating BAX/BAK to release cytochrome c, unlike confusables centred on apoptosome/SMAC, p53 transcription or BIM/BMF/BID.

name: N-glycan glucose addition, trimming and oligosaccharide catabolism
rationale: Members cover UDP-glucose and dolichyl-phosphate-glucose supply, MOGS/MAN1B1 glycan trimming and lysosomal oligosaccharide breakdown, unlike confusables on dolichol-oligosaccharide mannosylation or amino-sugar metabolism.

name: N-glycan glucosylation, trimming and oligosaccharide catabolism
rationale: Members concern glucose donors (UDP-glucose, dolichyl-phosphate-glucose), ER glucosidase/mannosidase trimming of N-glycans (MOGS, MAN1B1 defects) and lysosomal oligosaccharide breakdown, unlike confusables on dolichol-linked precursor assembly, GDP-mannose, UDP-GlcNAc or sialic acid metabolism.

qualifier: glucosyl donor supply and glucose/mannose trimming
name: Glucosyl donor synthesis and N-glycan trimming
rationale: Members link UDP-glucose and dolichyl-phosphate-glucose synthesis to N-glycan trimming (MOGS, MAN1B1) and oligosaccharide catabolism, unlike neighbours built around GlcNAc, mannose, sialic acid or the ALG lipid-linked assembly defects.

name: Urea cycle and arginine-citrulline-ornithine biosynthesis
rationale: All members are urea cycle metabolism of citrulline, ornithine and arginine and its transcriptional regulation, unlike the disease-variant, arginine catabolism and transport confusables.

name: Urea cycle operation and ornithine-citrulline-arginine biosynthesis
rationale: Members are the urea cycle, its transcriptional repression and citrulline/arginine/ornithine synthesis; confusables are urea cycle enzyme deficiencies or arginine catabolism and transport.

name: Urea cycle and arginine, citrulline and ornithine synthesis
rationale: Members are the urea cycle, its transcriptional repression and synthesis/metabolism of arginine, citrulline and ornithine, distinct from urea-cycle disease variants and arginine catabolism/transport confusables.

qualifier: aspartate transport and glutamate transporter disorders
name: Aspartate transport and glutamate transporter genetic disorders
rationale: All members concern aspartate/glutamate transporters (SLC1A1, SLC1A3, SLC17A8) and their diseases, unlike confusables on astrocytic glutamate reuptake or GABA transport.

qualifier: aspartate transport and excitatory amino acid transporter disease
name: Aspartate transport and excitatory amino acid transporter defects
rationale: All members involve glutamate/aspartate transporters (SLC1A1, SLC1A3, SLC17A8) or aspartate membrane transport; aspartate and transporter disease variants distinguish it from astrocytic glutamate reuptake and GABA confusables.

name: Aspartate/glutamate transporter defects and aspartate uptake
rationale: Members are aspartate import and inherited defects of glutamate/aspartate transporters (EAAT and vesicular glutamate), distinct from confusables on GABA/glycine transport and astrocytic glutamate reuptake.

name: Mitochondrial protein processing and calcium uptake regulation
rationale: Members cover intramitochondrial protein processing/turnover (including SMDT1 processing) plus regulation of mitochondrial calcium import, which the protein-import and cristae confusables lack.

name: Mitochondrial proteolysis and calcium uniporter regulation
rationale: All members concern intramitochondrial protein processing/catabolism or mitochondrial calcium uptake (including SMDT1/EMRE processing), which sets it apart from confusables on mitochondrial protein import, targeting and cristae formation.

name: Mitochondrial protein processing and calcium uptake regulation
rationale: Members share mitochondrial protein processing/turnover, and uniquely include SMDT1 processing and regulation of mitochondrial calcium import, which separates it from the protein-import and cristae confusables.

core: NOD-like receptor sensing of bacterial peptidoglycan
qualifier: with K63 ubiquitination and inflammasome signaling
name: NOD-like receptor peptidoglycan sensing via K63 ubiquitination and inflammasomes
rationale: All members concern innate detection of bacterial peptidoglycan/muramyl dipeptide by NOD1/2-type receptors; unlike the confusables (NOD regulation terms, TAK1/TLR cascades) the theme carries the inflammasome and K63-linked ubiquitination steps.

core: NOD-like receptor sensing of bacterial peptidoglycan
name: NOD-like receptor peptidoglycan sensing and inflammasome signaling
rationale: All members concern NOD1/2-type sensing of bacterial peptidoglycan/muramyl dipeptide and downstream innate signaling; inflammasome and K63-ubiquitination members distinguish it from the NOD1/NOD2-regulation and TAK1/JNK confusables.

name: NOD1/2 peptidoglycan sensing with K63-ubiquitin signaling
rationale: All members concern NOD-like receptor recognition of peptidoglycan/muramyl dipeptide and downstream antibacterial signaling; unlike the GO NOD-regulation confusables, the theme carries the NOD1/2 signaling cascade, K63 ubiquitination and inflammasome receptor members.

qualifier: with telomere maintenance and repair-coupled replication
name: DNA repair, damage response and telomere maintenance
rationale: Members cover every major DNA repair route (BER, NER, MMR, HR, NHEJ, TLS, ICL repair), damage checkpoints and telomere maintenance; this breadth distinguishes it from the chromatin-assembly, Cajal-body, cisplatin-response and replication-initiation neighbours.

qualifier: all repair modes plus telomere maintenance
name: Pan-pathway DNA repair and telomere maintenance
rationale: Members span base excision, nucleotide excision, mismatch, translesion, double-strand break repair and telomere maintenance, a far broader repair repertoire than the replication, chromatin assembly or telomerase-RNA confusables.

qualifier: excision, break and translesion repair plus telomere maintenance
name: Excision, break and translesion DNA repair with telomere maintenance
rationale: The 176 members cover essentially every DNA repair route (BER, NER, MMR, HR, NHEJ, TLS, crosslink and alkylation repair) together with telomere maintenance and replication-linked damage responses; closest confusables are narrower (double-strand break, replication initiation, chromatin assembly) and lack the excision repair and telomere members.

core: Oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase mutants and TKI resistance
name: Oncogenic KIT, PDGFR, ALK and FGFR mutants and TKI resistance
rationale: Members are cancer-associated RTK mutants, fusions and their TKI binding or resistance, centred on KIT, PDGFR, ALK and FGFR rather than the ERBB2, FLT3 or cytokine-receptor signaling of the confusables.

core: Oncogenic receptor tyrosine kinase mutants and inhibitor resistance
qualifier: KIT, PDGFR, ALK and FGFR rather than FLT3, ERBB2 or cytokine receptors
name: Oncogenic KIT, PDGFR, ALK, FGFR mutants and inhibitor resistance
rationale: Members are cancer mutants, fusions and TKI-resistant variants of class III and other RTKs (KIT, PDGFR, ALK, FGFR, LTK, FLT3 fusions), distinguishing the theme from FLT3-resistance, ERBB2-mutant and hematopoietic cytokine confusables.

qualifier: KIT, PDGFR, ALK, FGFR and TKI resistance
name: Oncogenic KIT, PDGFR, ALK, FGFR mutants and TKI resistance
rationale: All members are cancer-driving RTK mutants/fusions and their TKI binding or resistance; KIT, PDGFR, ALK and FGFR content distinguishes it from FLT3-resistance, ERBB2 and cytokine-receptor confusables.

qualifier: germinal center, memory and plasma cell
name: B lineage development, germinal center and plasma cell differentiation
rationale: Members are B cell signatures and development/differentiation terms through germinal center, memory and plasma cell stages (with Tfh/ICOS help), whereas confusables center on proximal BCR/TCR signaling, thymic T cell selection or isotype switching.

qualifier: germinal centre and plasma cell differentiation
name: B cell development, germinal centre and plasma cell differentiation
rationale: Members are B cell identity signatures, B cell proliferation/differentiation, germinal centre, Tfh/ICOS/CD27 help and plasma/memory cell programmes, unlike confusables centred on BCR signal transduction, isotype switching or T cell/thymic development.

qualifier: germinal centre, plasma and memory cell differentiation
name: B cell development and germinal centre, plasma, memory differentiation
rationale: Members are B cell lineage signatures and B cell development, proliferation, germinal centre, plasma and memory cell differentiation (with Tfh/ICOS help), whereas confusables centre on proximal BCR/TCR signalling, thymic T cell development or isotype switching.

qualifier: prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis and receptors
name: Prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis and receptor signaling
rationale: Members span COX/prostaglandin and leukotriene biosynthesis, PLA2 arachidonate release and prostanoid/leukotriene GPCRs, unlike neighbours on lipoxins/HETEs, P450 epoxygenase or histamine.

name: Prostaglandin and leukotriene synthesis and receptor signaling
rationale: Members cover cyclooxygenase prostanoid and leukotriene biosynthesis, their GPCRs and responses, separating it from lipoxin/HETE, P450 epoxygenase and histamine neighbours.

qualifier: cyclooxygenase prostanoid and leukotriene branches with their G protein-coupled receptors
name: Cyclooxygenase prostanoid and leukotriene synthesis with their receptors
rationale: Members cover arachidonate release, the COX/prostaglandin-thromboxane and leukotriene synthetic routes, their transport and catabolism, and the prostanoid, leukotriene and free fatty acid receptors that read them, unlike the cytochrome P450 epoxygenase/HETE, lipoxin and histamine confusables.

name: Fc-gamma receptor phagocytosis, cytotoxicity and inhibitory signaling
rationale: Members describe Fc-gamma receptor activation, phagocytosis, ADCC, hypersensitivity and inhibitory FcR/CD22 B cell regulation, versus BCR, neutrophil, Fc-epsilon mast cell and myeloid confusables.

name: Fc-gamma receptor phagocytosis and inhibitory immunoreceptor signaling
rationale: Members cover FCGR activation, phagocytic cup formation, ADCC, hypersensitivity and inhibitory CD22/SIRP/Fc signaling, unlike neighbours centered on mast-cell FcεRI and BCR activation or neutrophil inflammatory responses.

qualifier: activating phagocytosis and inhibitory co-receptor regulation
name: Fc-gamma receptor activating and inhibitory signaling in phagocytosis
rationale: Members cover FCGR activation, phagocytic cup formation, ADCC, hypersensitivity and inhibitory FcR/CD22/SIRP regulation, unlike confusables on BCR signaling, Fc-epsilon mast cell activation or neutrophil inflammation.

qualifier: viral DNA integration, latency and host transcriptional silencing
name: Viral DNA integration, latency and host transcriptional silencing
rationale: Members concern retroviral nuclear import and integration, HCMV events and latency, and host silencing or activation of viral and endogenous retroelement transcription (HUSH, KRAB-ZFP, ChAHP, APOBEC3G); integration and transcriptional silencing distinguish it from confusables on HIV entry/reverse transcription or RNA-virus replication.

core: Integrated and latent viral genome control
qualifier: DNA integration with host transcriptional silencing
name: Viral DNA integration, latency and host epigenetic transcriptional silencing
rationale: Members concern retroviral integration, herpesviral latency and host activation or silencing of viral/retroelement transcription; neighbours hold HIV entry/reverse transcription, RNA-virus replication or APOBEC editing.

core: Viral genome integration and host control of viral transcription
name: Viral DNA integration, latency and host transcriptional silencing
rationale: Members span retroviral integration and PIC import, HCMV events, viral latency and host activation/suppression of viral transcription including KRAB-ZFP, HUSH and ChAHP silencing; confusables hold HIV entry/reverse transcription or RNA-virus replication.

name: V-ATPase-driven acidification of lysosomes, endosomes and phagosomes
rationale: Members concern proton pumping and pH control in lysosomes, endosomes, Golgi and phagosomes (with phagolysosome fusion), the phagosomal members distinguishing it from pigment-granule and ion-exchanger confusables.

core: Organelle lumen pH regulation by V-ATPase
name: Endolysosomal and phagosomal lumen pH regulation
rationale: Members are V-ATPase-driven acidification and pH control of endosome, lysosome, Golgi and phagosome lumens including phagolysosome fusion, which the ion-exchanger, scramblase and pigmentation confusables lack.

name: V-ATPase acidification of lysosomes, endosomes and phagosomes
rationale: Members concern V-ATPase assembly and proton-driven acidification of lysosomal, endosomal, Golgi and phagosomal lumens; phagosome acidification and phagolysosome fusion distinguish it from ion-exchanger, pigmentation and scramblase neighbours.

qualifier: receptor-level FZD/LRP, DVL and AXIN regulation
name: Canonical Wnt signalosome: FZD/LRP, DVL and AXIN turnover
rationale: Members act at the membrane-proximal canonical Wnt step (FZD ubiquitination/RNF43, LRP5, DVL activation and degradation, AXIN degradation and recruitment, ligand antagonists), whereas confusables cover non-canonical Ca2+ Wnt, nuclear TCF/beta-catenin output or Wnt secretion.

name: Canonical Wnt receptor-proximal signaling and DVL/AXIN turnover
rationale: Members act at FZD/LRP5 receptors, ligand antagonists, DVL activation and AXIN/DVL degradation, unlike confusables on Wnt secretion, non-canonical calcium signaling or TCF/beta-catenin transcription.

name: Canonical Wnt receptor activation and AXIN/DVL turnover
rationale: Members cover Wnt-FZD/LRP signaling at the membrane, destruction complex disassembly and ubiquitin-mediated FZD, DVL and AXIN turnover, whereas confusables emphasise Wnt secretion, non-canonical calcium signaling or nuclear beta-catenin/TCF output.

core: Class I cytokine-type hormone receptor signaling
name: Growth hormone, prolactin and leptin receptor signaling
rationale: Members are GH, prolactin and leptin receptor signaling with IGF and body-growth regulation, unlike confusables on thyroid hormone, glucocorticoid or ghrelin/feeding control.

core: Class I cytokine hormone receptor signaling
name: Growth hormone, prolactin and leptin receptor signaling
rationale: Members are GH, prolactin and leptin receptor (JAK-STAT) signaling with IGF and body growth regulation, unlike thyroid, appetite and glucocorticoid confusables.

qualifier: growth hormone, prolactin and leptin; body growth
name: Growth hormone, prolactin and leptin receptor signaling
rationale: Members are GH, prolactin and leptin receptor JAK-STAT signaling and body growth regulation, unlike confusables on appetite/feeding, thyroid hormone or glucocorticoid secretion.

qualifier: preinitiation complex assembly and pause release, non-viral
name: RNA polymerase II preinitiation-to-elongation transition control
rationale: Members cover PIC assembly, promoter clearance, pausing and elongation complex formation, while confusables add HIV/Tat elongation and capping.

qualifier: host promoter clearance, preinitiation assembly and pausing, not HIV transcription
name: Regulation of RNA polymerase II promoter escape and pausing
rationale: All members concern Pol II promoter clearance, preinitiation complex assembly, pausing and early elongation; positive regulation of preinitiation assembly and transcription-factor control distinguish it from the HIV/Tat-centred and negative-elongation confusables.

name: Positive control of RNA polymerase II initiation and elongation
rationale: Members cover preinitiation complex assembly, promoter clearance, pausing and elongation complex formation with positive regulators, while confusables are dominated by HIV/Tat elongation and negative elongation control.

name: APC/C Cdc20-to-Cdh1 switch and late-mitotic substrate degradation
rationale: All members concern APC/C ubiquitin ligase activity during late mitosis/early G1, with the Cdh1 switch, Cdh1 autodegradation and Cdc6 removal distinguishing it from APC/C:Cdc20 metaphase-anaphase and Emi1 confusables.

core: APC/C substrate degradation at mitotic exit
name: APC/C-Cdh1 switch and substrate degradation at mitotic exit
rationale: Members describe APC/C ubiquitin-ligase activity in late mitosis/early G1, including the Cdc20-to-Cdh1 switch and Cdh1 autodegradation, distinct from confusables centred on APC/C:Cdc20 at metaphase-anaphase and Emi1/APC/C inhibition.

qualifier: Cdc20-to-Cdh1 switch and late mitosis/early G1 substrates
name: APC/C-Cdh1-mediated proteolysis at mitotic exit and early G1
rationale: All members concern regulation of the anaphase-promoting complex ubiquitin ligase and its substrate degradation during late anaphase into G1, with the Cdc20-to-Cdh1 switch and Cdh1 targets distinguishing it from confusables on APC/C:Cdc20 securin/cyclin B degradation, APC/C phosphorylation and Emi1 inhibition.

name: Regulation of ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal protein turnover
rationale: Members positively and negatively regulate ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis and protein destabilization, unlike confusables about ERAD/misfolded-protein quality control, degron pathways, chaperone folding or stress granules.

name: Regulation of proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent protein degradation
rationale: Members up- and down-regulate ubiquitin-dependent proteasomal proteolysis and protein destabilization, distinguishing it from confusables on protein folding/stabilization, ERAD and degron pathways or stress granules.

name: Regulation of ubiquitin-proteasome protein degradation
rationale: All members up- or down-regulate proteasomal ubiquitin-dependent catabolism (destabilization, autoubiquitination, UCH proteinases); confusables involve chaperone folding, degron rules, stress granules or ERAD.

name: Spindle orientation in forebrain neural progenitor division
rationale: Members pair astral microtubule and spindle positioning with forebrain neuroblast division and stem cell maintenance; C1 lacks the neural progenitor part, C3/C4 lack the spindle machinery.

name: Spindle orientation in asymmetric division of forebrain neural progenitors
rationale: Members link astral microtubule and spindle positioning to asymmetric division and proliferation of forebrain ventricular-zone neuroblasts and neural stem cells, unlike confusables limited to midbrain/forebrain patterning or centrosome positioning.

core: Spindle orientation in neural progenitor division
name: Spindle orientation in forebrain neural progenitor division
rationale: Members combine astral microtubule/spindle positioning and asymmetric division with forebrain neuroblast division and neural stem cell maintenance, which the centrosome-only and neuroblast-proliferation-only confusables each lack half of.

name: Homologous recombination repair by strand invasion and DNA synthesis
rationale: Members are recombinational repair steps (strand invasion, SDSA, sister chromatid exchange, repair synthesis, cross-link repair) rather than the NHEJ, damage-sensing, break-induced replication or telomere processes of the confusables.

name: Recombinational DNA repair by strand invasion and repair synthesis
rationale: Members describe recombination-based repair steps (strand invasion, SDSA, sister chromatid exchange, interstrand cross-link repair, repair DNA synthesis), distinct from confusables on NHEJ, BRCA1/2 damage signaling, Fanconi anemia or telomere/fork processes.

name: Recombinational DNA repair via strand invasion and synthesis
rationale: Members concern homologous recombination steps (strand invasion, SDSA, sister chromatid exchange, repair synthesis, cross-link repair), unlike confusables on NHEJ, damage sensing or BRCA defects.

qualifier: coupled to complex II and ATP synthesis
name: TCA cycle coupled to complex II and ATP synthesis
rationale: Members are TCA-cycle intermediates and steps plus succinate-ubiquinone electron transfer and ATP synthesis, distinguishing it from PDH/CoA, malate-aspartate shuttle and glutamate-metabolism confusables.

qualifier: coupled to succinate oxidation and ATP synthesis
name: TCA cycle coupled to succinate oxidation and ATP synthesis
rationale: Members are TCA intermediates (2-oxoglutarate, succinate, malate, pyruvate) plus complex II electron transfer and ATP synthase, distinguishing them from confusables about glutamate/aspartate anaplerosis, isocitrate/NADPH or PDH/CoA.

qualifier: coupled to succinate oxidation at complex II and ATP synthesis
name: TCA cycle linked to succinate oxidation and ATP synthesis
rationale: Members are TCA cycle intermediates (malate, succinate, 2-oxoglutarate) plus complex II electron transport and ATP synthesis, which distinguishes them from confusables built on isocitrate/NADPH, PDH/CoA, glutamate or the malate-aspartate shuttle.

name: Epithelial apical-basal polarity and adherens junction maintenance
rationale: All members concern epithelial polarity, apical constriction and adherens junction maintenance, distinguishing them from desmosome, adherens-junction assembly and podocyte confusables.

qualifier: adherens junction maintenance and apical constriction
name: Epithelial apical-basal polarity and adherens junction maintenance
rationale: All members concern establishing and maintaining epithelial apical-basal and cytoskeletal polarity with adherens-junction cell-cell adhesion, distinguishing it from podocyte, desmosome, adherens junction assembly and generic junction confusables.

qualifier: apical-basal polarity with adherens junction adhesion
name: Epithelial apical-basal polarity and adherens junction maintenance
rationale: All members concern establishing/maintaining epithelial apical-basal and cytoskeletal polarity, apical constriction and adherens-junction adhesion, unlike generic junction, desmosome, junction assembly or podocyte themes.

core: Mitochondrial branched-chain amino acid and lysine catabolism
qualifier: lipoate- and biotin-dependent enzymes and their deficiencies
name: Branched-chain amino acid and lysine catabolism with lipoate/biotin cofactors
rationale: Members cover leucine, isoleucine, valine and lysine catabolism via lipoylated 2-oxoacid dehydrogenases and biotin-dependent carboxylases with their inborn errors (MSUD, organic acidemias, biotinidase deficiency), unlike TCA cycle, serine/B6 and CoA/PDH regulation confusables.

core: Mitochondrial amino acid and short-chain acyl-CoA catabolism
name: Branched-chain and lysine catabolism with lipoyl and biotin cofactors
rationale: Members cover mitochondrial branched-chain amino acid and lysine catabolism, 2-oxoacid dehydrogenase complexes, biotin-dependent carboxylases, protein lipoylation and their inborn organic acidemias, which TCA cycle, CoA synthesis and serine/B6 neighbours lack.

qualifier: organic acidemias with biotin and lipoyl cofactor defects
name: Branched-chain amino acid catabolism and biotin/lipoyl cofactor disorders
rationale: Members cover BCAA, lysine and short-chain acyl-CoA catabolism, 2-oxoacid dehydrogenases, protein lipoylation, biotin-dependent carboxylases and their inborn errors (MSUD, isovaleric acidemia), which the vitamin B6 (C1), TCA cycle (C2, C3) and CoA/PDH regulation (C4) neighbours lack.

qualifier: mtDNA replication, transcription, RNA processing and translation
name: Mitochondrial genome replication, transcription and translation
rationale: Nearly all members concern mitochondrial DNA replication/repair, transcription, RNA processing/stability, ribosome assembly and translation, unlike confusables limited to RNA pseudouridylation/methylation or nuclear tRNA processing.

qualifier: mtDNA replication, transcription, RNA processing and translation
name: Mitochondrial genome replication, transcription and translation
rationale: Nearly all members cover mtDNA replication and repair, mitochondrial transcription, RNA processing/stability and mitoribosome translation, whereas confusables focus on nuclear tRNA processing or RNA modification chemistry.

qualifier: mtDNA replication and transcription through translation
name: Mitochondrial genome replication, transcription, RNA processing and translation
rationale: Members span mtDNA replication/repair, mitochondrial transcription, RNA processing and stability, mitoribosome assembly and translation, whereas confusables cover generic RNA modification or nuclear tRNA processing.

name: Inflammasome activation, pyroptosis and IL-1/IL-18 maturation
rationale: Members are canonical (NLRP1/3, AIM2, IPAF) and noncanonical caspase-4/5 inflammasomes, pyroptotic death and IL-1/IL-18 processing and signaling, which TLR/LPS and IL-17 confusables lack.

name: Inflammasome assembly, pyroptosis and IL-1/IL-18 maturation
rationale: Members are canonical and non-canonical (caspase-4/5) inflammasomes, pyroptosis and IL-1/IL-18 processing and signaling, which the TLR/NOD, IL-17 and chemokine confusables lack.

name: Inflammasome assembly, pyroptosis and IL-1/IL-18 maturation
rationale: Members are canonical and non-canonical inflammasomes (NLRP1/3, AIM2, IPAF, CASP4/5), pyroptosis and IL-1/IL-18 processing; neighbours are TLR/NOD signaling, IL-17/IL-36 and chemokine production without inflammasome machinery.

qualifier: IL-2, IL-3 family cytokines and FLT3 with CBL control
name: STAT5 signalling by IL-2, IL-3 family cytokines and FLT3
rationale: Members are IL-2, IL-7, IL-9, IL-3 and IL-5 signalling and FLT3 signalling with CBL-mediated attenuation converging on STAT5, unlike confusables centred on IL-15/IL-21, IL-6/CSF1, erythropoietin/thrombopoietin or Th2/mast cell cytokines.

name: Interleukin and FLT3 receptor STAT5 signalling
rationale: Members are IL-2, IL-7, IL-9, IL-3 and IL-5 signalling, STAT5 activation, and FLT3/CBL/CSF3 signalling and its negative regulation, unlike confusables centred on IL-6/IL-10 families, Th2/mast cell effector biology, M-CSF or erythropoietin/thrombopoietin.

qualifier: IL-2/7/9/3/5 and FLT3 with CBL regulation
name: STAT5-activating interleukin and FLT3 signalling with CBL regulation
rationale: Members are IL-2, IL-7, IL-9, IL-3 and IL-5 receptor signalling, STAT5 activation and FLT3/G-CSF signalling with CBL-mediated attenuation, unlike IL-15/21, EPO/TPO or IL-6/CSF1 confusables.

qualifier: oncogene, replicative and stress-induced, with heterochromatin and Polycomb silencing
name: Oncogene, replicative and stress-induced senescence with heterochromatin silencing
rationale: All members concern induction and regulation of cellular senescence; the theme adds SAHF/subtelomeric heterochromatin and BMI1 Polycomb silencing plus SASP, whereas confusables centre on p53 apoptotic control or cancer evasion of senescence via p16/p14ARF defects.

qualifier: heterochromatin foci, Polycomb silencing and secretory phenotype
name: Cellular senescence with heterochromatin foci and secretory phenotype
rationale: All members concern induction and regulation of oncogene-, stress- and replication-induced senescence, distinguished by SAHF/Polycomb chromatin silencing and the SASP, whereas confusables focus on p53 apoptosis, UV response or cancer evasion of senescence.

qualifier: stress- and oncogene-induced, with heterochromatin and Polycomb silencing
name: Stress- and oncogene-induced senescence with heterochromatin silencing
rationale: All members concern entry into and regulation of senescence (oncogene, oxidative, replicative), its SASP and its chromatin basis (SAHF, Polycomb BMI1 modules), whereas confusables centre on cancer evasion of senescence via p16/p14ARF defects or p53 DNA-damage and UV responses.

qualifier: renin-angiotensin and vasoactive peptide control of natriuresis
name: Renin-angiotensin and vasoactive peptide control of natriuresis and pressure
rationale: Members cover angiotensin generation and signaling, bradykinin/neuropeptide catabolism and guanylyl cyclase cGMP control of renal sodium excretion and blood pressure, unlike confusables on nitric oxide and vascular smooth muscle contraction.

core: Renin-angiotensin control of blood pressure and volume
qualifier: angiotensin and bradykinin peptide processing with renal sodium handling
name: Renin–angiotensin peptide processing and renal blood volume control
rationale: Members cover angiotensin generation and signaling, bradykinin/neuropeptide catabolism, natriuretic cGMP signaling and renal sodium and volume regulation of pressure, unlike NO-cGMP vascular and smooth-muscle confusables.

core: Renin-angiotensin blood pressure and volume regulation
qualifier: vasoactive peptide processing and renal natriuresis
name: Renin-angiotensin and vasoactive peptide control of blood volume and natriuresis
rationale: Members concern angiotensin generation and signaling, bradykinin/neuropeptide catabolism and natriuretic cGMP signaling in renal sodium, urine volume and blood pressure control; confusables focus on nitric oxide/eNOS, smooth muscle contraction or neural/endothelin pressure regulation.

name: Chylomicron and VLDL remodeling and clearance
rationale: Members cover lipase-mediated remodelling and clearance of chylomicrons and VLDL, distinct from LDL/HDL remodelling, intestinal lipid absorption/assembly and LXR transcriptional neighbours.

name: Chylomicron and VLDL lipolytic remodeling and clearance
rationale: Members concern LPL/LIPC assembly and chylomicron/VLDL remodeling and clearance, unlike confusables on LDL/HDL remodeling or intestinal lipid absorption.

name: Lipase-mediated chylomicron and VLDL remodelling and clearance
rationale: Members cover LPL/hepatic lipase assembly and chylomicron/VLDL remodelling and clearance with their regulation; distinct from intestinal absorption, HDL/LDL remodelling and LXR lipogenesis confusables.

qualifier: PTEN control by ceRNAs and localization, and oncogenic AKT activation
name: PTEN-AKT axis: ceRNA control and oncogenic disruption
rationale: Members concern PTEN-dependent restraint of PI3K/AKT (ceRNA/lncRNA control of PTEN, PTEN localization, IGF receptor dampening) and its oncogenic loss or AKT1 E17K activation, distinguishing them from PTEN stability/ERBB2 and inositol phosphate confusables.

name: PTEN-AKT signaling axis and noncoding-RNA control of PTEN
rationale: Members concern PTEN restraint of PI3K/AKT, oncogenic AKT1/PTEN loss and ceRNA/lncRNA regulation of PTEN, distinguishing it from PTEN stability, ERBB2/3, TORC2 and nuclear phosphoinositide confusables.

name: PTEN-mediated restraint of PI3K/AKT signaling, including ceRNA control
rationale: Members concern PTEN loss, localization and ceRNA/lncRNA translational control, negative PI3K/AKT and IGF receptor regulation and AKT targets, while confusables cover inositol phosphate synthesis, PTEN stability or ERBB2/3 downregulation.

qualifier: von Willebrand factor-GPIb-IX-V axis and its variants
name: Von Willebrand factor-GPIb platelet adhesion to collagen
rationale: Members describe VWF binding to collagen and GPIb-IX-V, its ADAMTS13 cleavage and disease variants, and resulting platelet activation, unlike neighbours on platelet aggregation, collagen-integrin matrix, fibrin coagulation or factor XII contact activation.

qualifier: von Willebrand factor-GPIb axis and its disease variants
name: Von Willebrand factor-GPIb platelet adhesion and its disease variants
rationale: Members cover VWF binding to GPIb-IX-V and collagen, ADAMTS13 cleavage and their variants, unlike basement-membrane, aggregation, coagulation or contact-pathway neighbours.

qualifier: GPIb-IX-V binding, collagen and ADAMTS13 cleavage variants
name: Von Willebrand factor platelet adhesion and ADAMTS13 cleavage
rationale: Members cover VWF binding to collagen and GPIb-IX-V, platelet adhesion and activation, and VWF/GP1BA/ADAMTS13 variants; the GPIb-VWF axis separates it from basement-membrane, contact-activation and coagulation-cascade neighbours.

name: AMPA and kainate receptor excitatory transmission
rationale: Members are AMPA and Na-/Ca-permeable kainate receptor activation, excitatory transmission, short-term plasticity and kainate-induced neuron death, unlike confusables on NMDA receptors, presynaptic kainate/GABA or AMPA trafficking.

name: Kainate and AMPA receptor excitatory transmission and excitotoxicity
rationale: Members are AMPA and kainate receptor activation, excitatory transmission, short-term plasticity and kainate-induced hippocampal neuron death, unlike presynaptic kainate/GABA and NMDA-focused confusables.

name: Postsynaptic kainate and AMPA receptor activation and excitotoxicity
rationale: Members describe kainate and AMPA receptor activation in excitatory transmission and kainate-induced hippocampal neuron death, whereas confusables cover presynaptic kainate/G-protein effects, AMPA trafficking or NMDA receptor signaling.

qualifier: IKK complex recruitment by IRAK1 and RIP1
name: IKK complex recruitment and canonical NF-kappaB activation
rationale: Members concern IRAK1/RIP1-mediated IKK recruitment and positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB, distinct from TAK1 activation, IRF3/7 and TNFR1 confusables.

core: IKK complex recruitment for canonical NF-kappaB activation
name: IRAK1- and RIP1-mediated IKK recruitment to NF-kappaB
rationale: Members describe IKK complex recruitment by IRAK1 or RIP1 and positive regulation of canonical NF-kappaB, unlike confusables centred on TAK1 activation, IRF3/7 activation or TNFR1 signaling.

qualifier: IKK complex recruitment downstream of TLRs
name: TLR-driven IKK recruitment and canonical NF-kappaB activation
rationale: Members describe IRAK1/RIP1-mediated IKK complex recruitment and NF-kappaB regulation, distinguishing it from TAK1, TBK1-IRF and TNFR1 confusables.

name: Threonine catabolism within L-amino acid metabolism
rationale: Members are threonine catabolism and the general amino acid metabolic terms containing it, distinguishing the theme from glycine/glyoxylate, proline and acyl-conjugation confusables.

name: Threonine and L-amino acid catabolism
rationale: Members are threonine catabolism and general L-amino acid metabolism/catabolism, distinguishing it from glycine conjugation, glycine/glyoxylate and proline confusables.

name: Threonine-centred amino acid catabolism
rationale: Members are threonine metabolism/catabolism plus general L-amino acid catabolic terms, unlike glycine, proline or acid-conjugation confusables.

qualifier: FGFR1 and FGFR2 via FRS, SHC and PLC
name: FGFR1 and FGFR2 signaling via FRS and SHC adaptors
rationale: All members are FRS-, SHC- or PLC-mediated cascades from FGFR1/FGFR2, unlike confusables covering PI3K cascades, FGFR4/betaKlotho, ligand binding or oncogenic mutants.

name: FRS2/SHC adaptor signaling downstream of FGFR1 and FGFR2
rationale: All members are FRS-, SHC- or PLC-mediated cascades of FGFR1/FGFR2; confusables hold ligand binding, activating mutants, FGFR4 or PI3K cascades instead.

qualifier: via FRS2, SHC and PLC-gamma adaptors
name: FRS2, SHC and PLC-gamma cascades downstream of FGFR1/FGFR2
rationale: All members are adaptor-mediated (FRS, SHC, PLC) cascades from FGFR1 or FGFR2, separating the theme from FGFR4/betaKlotho, FGFR mutant activation, ligand-binding and PI3K-cascade themes.

name: Pinocytic uptake and onward early endosome cargo routing
rationale: Members regulate pinocytosis, cargo arrival at early endosomes and onward transport to late or recycling endosomes and transcytosis; confusables emphasize receptor recycling, macropinocytic ruffling or Golgi-endosome traffic.

name: Pinocytic uptake and early endosome cargo routing
rationale: Members concern pinocytosis and onward routing of cargo from early endosomes to late or recycling endosomes and transcytosis, unlike confusables on macropinocytic protrusions, Golgi-endosome transport, receptor recycling or GLUT4 translocation.

name: Pinocytic uptake, early endosome routing and transcytosis
rationale: Members regulate pinocytosis, early endosome localization and onward transport to late or recycling endosomes and transcytosis, unlike macropinocytosis, receptor recycling or Golgi trafficking neighbours.

name: Peroxisomal beta-oxidation of straight and branched-chain fatty acids
rationale: Members are acyl-CoA oxidase beta-oxidation of very-long, long, medium-chain and branched (pristanoyl-CoA) fatty acids, unlike confusables on alpha-oxidation, ABCD1/peroxisome maintenance or essential fatty acid metabolism.

name: Peroxisomal beta-oxidation of long, medium and branched-chain fatty acids
rationale: Members describe acyl-CoA oxidase beta-oxidation of very long, long, medium and branched (pristanoyl) chains, distinct from confusables on ABCD1/peroxisome maintenance, alpha-oxidation or short-chain catabolism.

name: Beta-oxidation of medium, long and branched-chain fatty acids
rationale: Members are fatty acid beta-oxidation across medium, long, very long and branched (pristanoyl) chains, distinguishing it from confusables on ALD/VLCFA-CoA catabolism, alpha-oxidation and peroxisome maintenance.

name: NGF-TRKA and p75NTR survival and death signaling
rationale: Members are NGF/TRKA cascades plus p75NTR and dependence-receptor death signalling, which the NTRK2/NTRK3-centred confusables lack.
